Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? ## Applied Computing — Master of Science

This is a **full-time, two-year, in-person master’s program** focused on applying advanced computing methods to complex, real-world problems. It is offered through the **School of Computing and Academic Studies**, primarily at the Burnaby campus, with possible activities at the Downtown Campus or field locations.

The cohort-based curriculum combines computer science, information technology, applied research, and an application area such as building science, biotechnology, sustainability, autonomous vehicles, rehabilitation engineering, smart micro-grids, or network security.

### Program structure

The first year establishes the common technical and research foundation:

**September–December**
- **COMP 9060 — Applied Algorithm Analysis** — 3 credits
- **COMP 9170 — Data Science** — 3 credits
- **COMP 9200 — Applied Research Methods** — 3 credits

**January–April**
- **COMP 9040 — Human-centered Computing** — 3 credits
- **COMP 9080 — Research Proposal** — 0 credits
- **COMP 9130 — Applied Artificial Intelligence** — 3 credits
- **COMP 9150 — Cyber Security for Applied Computing** — 3 credits

An approved **COMP 9190 — Application Area Directed Studies** course may replace **COMP 9130 — Applied Artificial Intelligence**, **COMP 9150 — Cyber Security for Applied Computing**, or **COMP 9170 — Data Science**.

### Second-year choice

Students choose exactly one of two paths:

1. **Thesis Path**
   - **COMP 9600 — M.Sc. Thesis** — 12 credits  
   This involves completing and defending an original applied research thesis. It is the path most aligned with possible future doctoral study.

2. **Project & Internship Path**
   - **COMP 9290 — Special Topics in Applied Computing** — 3 credits
   - **COMP 9400 — Industry Internship** — 6 credits
   - **COMP 9500 — M.Sc. Research Project** — 3 credits  
   The internship may be paid or unpaid and can take place with an external organization or a BCIT lab.

Before beginning either the thesis or research project, students must maintain at least a **70% average across all program courses**. The normal completion time is two academic years, with a maximum permitted completion time of five years.

### Entrance profile

Admission is competitive. Applicants must meet the English requirement of **English Studies 12 at 67% or an accepted equivalent** and qualify through one of these routes:

- **Standard entry:** a bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent, with at least **2.8/4.0 or 70% over the final 30 undergraduate credits**.
- **Alternate entry:** a bachelor’s degree in another discipline, with at least **3.0/4.0 or 73% over the final 30 credits**, plus significant computing knowledge. This route requires program-area review and may involve bridging courses.

A mandatory applicant questionnaire, two references, complete supporting documentation, and competitive review by the Graduate Program Committee are also required. Relevant industry experience is preferred but has no stored minimum threshold.

The program accepts international applicants. A valid study permit is required before starting, and graduates currently meet the program-based condition to apply for a post-graduation work permit; final eligibility and approval remain with IRCC.

The stored program information states that the **September 2026 intake is closed** and applications for **September 2027 open October 1, 2026**.

[View the Applied Computing Master of Science program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/applied-computing-master-of-science-full-time-m600msc/)
